service_at_issue: home health skilled nursing visits (mediplanner filling) and home health aide services, Oct 2005 to Sept 2006
facts: The beneficiary began receiving home health care from the provider in June 2001, more than four years before the initial date of service at issue.

The beneficiary’s primary diagnosis was type I diabetes mellitus (without mention of complication and not stated as uncontrolled), and his other diagnoses included hypertension, venous thrombosis, coronary atherosclerosis of unspecified type, glaucoma, and chronic renal failure.
During the periods of service at issue, a skilled nurse visited the beneficiary approximately once every two weeks to fill a mediplanner with pills and oversee home health aides.
Concurrently, a home health aide visited the beneficiary five days each week, averaging 30-35 hours a week, to assist with personal care, light housekeeping, and meal preparation.

the appellant-provider asserts that there were no physician orders for skilled services during the periods in question and that skilled “observation and assessment” services cannot occur for over a 50-week period.
The beneficiary did not receive any skilled rehabilitation therapy during the period of service at issue.
the plans of care on file reveal physician’s orders for the skilled nurse to “visit Q 2 weeks to pour mediplanner.”
The plans of care do not contain physician’s orders for observation and assessment and the nursing notes do not reveal any significant changes in the beneficiary’s status or condition.
outcome_note: The Council reversed the ALJ, finding pouring a mediplanner is not a skilled service and nothing supported skilled observation and assessment, so the aide services were also non-covered and the provider was liable.
